resources.string: Lets this study record interaction events, the raw on-screen bounds and type of the interacted accessibility element, and derived screen regions. Element bounds are not your exact finger coordinates. Chronicle never reads the text of what you tap, type, or read, never captures screen contents, and does not intercept touch input. Collection only happens while you are enrolled and have agreed to share Interaction Events; you can turn it off here at any time.

Chronicle is not an accessibility tool. If you continue and enable its service in Android Accessibility settings, Chronicle can record tap, scroll, focus, and element-type events, including the raw on-screen bounds of the interacted accessibility element, derived screen regions, and the foreground app package. These research records are encrypted on this device and uploaded to the enrolled study server shown during enrollment for the authorized research team. The bounds are not your exact finger coordinates. Chronicle does not intercept touch input or collect typed text, visible text, content descriptions, or screenshots, and does not sell or use this data for advertising. You can cancel now or turn the service off later. Android will show the Accessibility settings screen next.

Effective and last updated October 7, 2026.

Scope and responsibility. Chronicle is a reusable research data-collection app. The app publisher maintains the Android client. Each research study is separately responsible for its protocol, participant consent, server, retention rules, disclosures, contacts, and participant rights. A participant can have only one active Chronicle study on a device at a time.

Information Chronicle may handle. An enrolled study supplies a study identifier and participant reference. Chronicle creates a device-instance identifier and records consent choices. Enrollment also sends the device model, manufacturer, and Android version. Depending on the modules the study requests and the participant accepts, this non-Play research variant may collect app package names and usage timing; in-app activity class names; device lifecycle, battery, storage, thermal, connectivity, settings, and per-app network byte-count data; hardware sensor measurements; physical-activity and sleep events; notification source, category, timing, and event metadata; media title, artist, and album metadata and audio playback state; content-free tap, scroll, focus, element-role, and on-screen-bounds events; participant category selections; and read-only Health Connect records.

Information Chronicle does not collect. Chronicle does not collect precise location, contacts, messages, typed text, notification text, websites or search terms, screenshots, photos, videos, microphone recordings, advertising identifiers, financial information, or advertising profiles. It contains no advertising or cross-app tracking SDK.

Purpose and sharing. Information is used only to operate the enrolled research protocol, monitor collection and data quality, secure and troubleshoot the service, prevent unauthorized or duplicate requests, honor withdrawal and deletion, and meet the obligations stated by the study. Chronicle does not sell research data or use it for advertising, marketing, credit, insurance, or medical decisions. Data is sent only to the one public HTTPS server identified by the active study. If the physical-activity or sleep module is accepted, Chronicle uses Google Play services (Activity Recognition and Sleep API), which runs on the device under Google's own terms, to detect those events; Chronicle uploads the resulting events only to the study server.

Background operation and permissions. Accepted modules may collect and upload on a schedule while the app is closed. Android may show an ongoing foreground-service notification for collection that requires it. Usage Access, Notification Listener, Accessibility, Activity Recognition, and Health Connect access are requested only for accepted modules and can be revoked in Android settings.

Storage, security, retention, withdrawal, and deletion. Pending research records and enrollment credentials are encrypted on the device and sent over an authenticated encrypted connection to the active study server. Participants can review module status in Data Sharing. To withdraw from Chronicle collection, uninstall the app; Android then removes Chronicle's on-device app data. Use Withdraw from study in Chronicle Settings to stop collection and request withdrawal from the enrolled study server. Keep the app installed and connected until the request is acknowledged. Chronicle then clears local enrollment and pending records. Contact your study team about records already uploaded and any additional deletion options. Server retention and participant rights are controlled by the study consent and approved protocol.

Contact. Questions about participation, research records, retention, or rights should go to the research team named by the active study. Questions about the Chronicle Android application or publisher-level privacy inquiries may be sent to uzairalam998@gmail.com. Baylor College of Medicine general institutional privacy policy is available at https://www.bcm.edu/privacy.

Upload delivery diagnostics. Chronicle reports bounded daily aggregates of upload success, failure, retry, collection-access loss, and crash counts, including HTTP status and bounded exception class where available. These diagnostics exclude research content, participant labels, credentials, server URLs, free-form error text, and stack traces. Diagnostics follow study retention and explicit enrollment erasure.

Children and study eligibility. Chronicle is not a general consumer service for children. A minor may participate only under an approved study protocol with any required parent or guardian permission and participant assent.
